what_changed.why_6: Each draw is 3 samples. With r the per-draw resolve probability, expected draws per species is (1 - r**A) / (1 - r): at r~=0.5 that is 1.75 at A=3, 1.94 at A=5, 1.97 at A=6, 2.0 as A grows -- draws past ~3 buy tail coverage almost for free. The worst case stays bounded at 3A calls (18 at A=6) against the 120 node calls one species already costs, and 6 is the smallest round bound that leaves under ~2% of a roster unresolved at r~=0.5. Reaching the bound is recorded by name, never silently retried.

second_reading_interrupted_run.why_kept: It is a second, independent set of 6 first draws (pooled with the completed run: 8 of 14 first draws resolved = 0.571), and it is the evidence for the species-dependence question below: ArmoredImpZombie resolved on draw 2 here and on draw 4 in the completed run, while AbyssSwordStar and AcientSunNut resolved on draw 1 in both.

interpretation: One invocation now converges: all 8 species of the slice left a species/<id>.json, 8 with a resolved codex sentence and 0 with a named failure, so there is no silent gap to confuse with a model refusal. The vote is confirmed stochastic at roughly one resolve per two draws (pooled 8 of 13 draws this run; 8 of 14 first draws including the interrupted run) -- the J9-B2 reading reproduces with a larger n and a slightly better point estimate than the 2-species/4-draw proof that filed the row. Nothing in this fix explains WHY the draw fails: the retry converges around the flakiness, it does not remove it.
species_dependence: NOT proved either way with n=1 species observed twice. The one species observed in two runs (ArmoredImpZombie: draw 2, then draw 4) moved, and the two species observed in both runs at draw 1 (AbyssSwordStar, AcientSunNut) stayed. That weakly favours a per-draw stochastic property over a per-species difficulty, but two observations cannot separate them; a per-species difficulty and a per-draw draw would look identical at this n.

residual_projection.basis: Measured per-draw rate 8/13 = 0.615 (Wilson 95% CI about 0.36-0.82). Residual after the default bound of 6 draws is (1 - r)**6.
residual_projection.observed: the furthest any species went was 4 draws (ArmoredImpZombie), 0 of 8 reached the bound
residual_projection.cheap_resume: a species that does reach the bound is re-drawable for 3 model calls (its 40 nodes are already in the shared ledger), so the tail is a short second pass over a NAMED list, not a re-run of the roster

release_reading: The 840/904-species run can be released. One invocation now converges in the sense the row asked for -- every species in a slice ends with either a resolved codex summary or a named, bounded failure -- and the measured tail is small: 0 of 8 failed at the default bound, the worst species took 4 draws, and any failures are enumerable from the species files and cheap to resume. The residual is NOT zero and the projection is wide at n=13 draws; if BCU2.12's own run leaves more than a handful of named failures, the choices are a resume pass over the named list (3 calls each) or raising --codex-attempts, which the driver already exposes.
not_proved: WHY the vote fails at roughly 4 draws in 10. Candidates are the 600-per-mille single-linkage rung (J9-B1(a)'s choice), the 3-sample count, and the prompt; none was isolated, and this fix deliberately does not change any of them.
Whether the per-draw resolve rate depends on the species. One species observed twice moved (draw 2 -> draw 4); the sample is too small to separate a per-species difficulty from a per-draw draw.
Whether the rate is stable across roster position, element/aptitude cell, or model load. All 8 species here are the first 8 of _index.json and share the same local model instance.
The residual failure count at 840/904 scale. The projection above is a CI over 13 measured draws, not a measurement of the roster.
How an unresolved codexSummary surfaces to a player (the Codex card's own rendering) -- no consumer of species/<id>.json with a null codexSummary was exercised here.

Whether a hard model/transport failure during a retry draw is named as well as a vote failure. A retry exception lands in run_batch's existing per-species `error` row; the unit tests cover the vote path, not a transport failure mid-retry.
